deals.date_text: Financing plan set out 17 December 2024; project stalled by litigation since October 2025
deals.evidence: ils seront prioritairement mobilisés pour rembourser l’emprunt bancaire de 39M€
deals.headline: Arkéa Park: EUR 39m bank loan in a ~EUR 106m new-stadium plan
deals.investor: Bank lenders (not named) to the Arkéa Park project company
deals.source_name: Stade Brestois 29 press release (project holders), 17 December 2024
deals.summary: The project holders (the Le Saint brothers) describe Arkéa Park, a 15,000-seat stadium planned in Guipavas, as mostly privately financed with public participation (Région Bretagne, Département du Finistère, Brest métropole) and a target budget of nearly EUR 106m; the project company's results would go first to repaying a EUR 39m bank loan, and all operating revenue (rents) would go to the club. An administrative court ruling in October 2025 halted the works; Brest métropole, the prefecture and the département said they maintained the project.

stadium_owner.detail: A Brest métropole sports facility (listed among the metropole's équipements sportifs), occupied by the club; the club's own December 2024 statement says a renovation of Le Blé would have been paid entirely by Brest taxpayers. The planned replacement, Arkéa Park in Guipavas, would also sit on Brest métropole land and pass to the metropole at the end of a building lease.

notes: Revenue is DNCG's total non-transfer earnings for 2024-25 (EUR 94,936k, the Champions League season); the SA's own statutory turnover for the year is EUR 90.7m and net profit EUR 6.04m (French register). 2025-26 accounts not yet published. Breakdown uses DNCG categories. No valuation found: no transaction, no Forbes entry. The Le Saint stake (99%) is from ICI/Radio France (June 2026); no registry or club page states the split between the brothers. Shirt sponsor not stated on a page read (Crédit Mutuel Arkéa is a major partner and the naming partner of the planned stadium). No chief executive on a page read with a current date: the French register lists Gérard Le Saint as directeur général délégué; the club calls him vice-president of the board. Stadium capacity: the club gives 15,220; Brest métropole gives 16,160 spectators including 15,333 seated. Honours not recorded (no league title; no page read that states the club's honours list). No dated social follower count found.

owners.evidence: les frères Le Saint, qui détiennent depuis dix ans 99% des parts du Stade Brestois
owners.name: Denis and Gérard Le Saint (Le Saint family)

ownership_summary: Stade Brestois 29 SA is owned by brothers Denis and Gérard Le Saint, who run the family fruit, vegetable and fish wholesaler Le Saint; they hold 99% and have done for about ten years (ICI/Radio France, June 2026). Denis Le Saint has been president since May 2016. In 2026 he said for the first time that he was open to selling or bringing in investors; no transaction had been announced in the sources read.
